pages.text: With Time in my veins I can bend it.$(br2)$(l)Rewind$() (level 1): I am back where I stood five seconds ago. Only my place: my wounds stay.$(br2)$(l)Slow Time$() (level 2): the chunk I stand in runs at half speed, or a quarter, or an eighth. Creatures, furnaces, crops, water, its very sun.

$(l)Time Freeze$() (level 3): the chunk stops. Arrows hang in the air, water stands mid-fall, the sun does not move.$(br2)Both last until I use the power again, run out of Time, or walk away. The chunk does not snap back: it races to catch up, then slows, landing exactly on the world's hour and the moon's phase.
pages.title: Stopping It

pages.text: Anyone in the chunk without the $(l)full Chrono-Insulated Suit$() is caught in it, me included. Suited, I keep the world's time: I walk through my own slowed chunk at my own pace.$(br2)Frozen, a body cannot move or act at all.
pages.title: Who It Holds

pages.text: Light is slowed with everything else. From outside, a slowed chunk looks $(l)red and dim$(): its light arrives tired. A stopped chunk lets no light out and none through: a $(l)black column$() shaped like the chunk, with a thin glow where light only grazes it. Caught inside, the world outside looks blue and racing.$(br2)Through the suit's goggles, a stopped chunk is an old photograph instead.
pages.title: How It Looks
A Minute's Rest
pages.text: Time does not like being bent. Once I let go of a slowed or stopped chunk (or it is torn from me), that power will not answer again for a minute.
